page: Microsoft Azure F2as_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Fasv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs utilizing the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The CPU configuration includes 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, though it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core performance, with the stress-ng single-core CPU test scoring 3080.07 and the Geekbench single-core test reaching 2056.0, both placing in the top 25% of tested servers. Single-threaded text processing and bzip3 decompression also demonstrate strong performance. However, multi-core and multi-threaded benchmarks, such as the Geekbench multi-core score of 3781.0 and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression at 27.03 GB/sec, fall into the bottom 25%. Memory read bandwidth is also weak, with large block read-only bandwidth measured at 38.2 GB/sec.

The F2as_v6 offers a dedicated CPU allocation with advanced instruction support, including AVX-512 and cryptography acceleration. While single-core compute capabilities are robust, the overall resource density is limited by the 2-vCPU ceiling and weak memory read performance, which constrains its suitability for memory-intensive or highly parallelized workloads. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for entry-level workloads requiring dedicated CPU cycles without local storage needs. Suitable workloads include lightweight single-threaded applications, basic text processing, and small-scale general-purpose tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure F2as_v6 is an x86_64 general-purpose virtual machine from the Fasv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor clocked at 3.7 GHz, paired with 8.0 GB of system memory. The instance does not include local storage or GPUs but is Premium Storage capable. Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores ranking in the top 25%. Conversely, multi-core performance, memory read bandwidth, and database operations fall into the bottom 25%. This hardware profile is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that rely on single-threaded execution and dedicated CPU allocation, such as lightweight text processing, basic web serving, and entry-level general-purpose applications, while being less suited for memory-intensive or highly parallelized tasks.
